queries: Jensen Huang China chips lobbying November 2026

sources_considered.why: Full text reports Huang's remarks at a press session attended by the publication.
Full text quotes Huang explicitly hoping China would permit sales; it attributes the remarks to Bloomberg.
Full Reuters report provides a material qualification about Chinese government restrictions.
Read in full. Corroborates lobbying but relies partly on anonymous accounts; the selected quotations more directly establish demand and Huang's stated preference.

evidence_items.locator: Third body paragraph, CES press-session remarks

receipt.public_excerpt: "The customer demand is high. It’s quite high. It’s very high," Huang said.

evidence_items.explanation: The surrounding passage identifies the demand as Chinese customer demand for H200 chips. This is Huang's assessment, reported by journalists attending the session, rather than an independently audited order count.

receipt.public_excerpt: "I’m hoping that the Chinese government would allow Nvidia to sell the H200," Huang reportedly said.

evidence_items.explanation: Huang expressly favored permission to sell H200 chips in China. A news account is used because a readable company transcript of these remarks was not located.

evidence_items.locator: Body paragraph immediately before the requests-for-comment paragraph

receipt.public_excerpt: But Beijing has yet to approve large-volume imports into China, the people said.

evidence_items.explanation: Chinese government restrictions qualify any reading that treats China as a single actor uniformly favoring imports. They do not negate demand among Chinese customers.

unresolved_gaps: These sources do not establish that the Chinese government uniformly wanted unrestricted imports.
They do not establish any connection between Huang's sales advocacy and the personal or intelligence allegations in the surrounding post.
